To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) in peer-assisted systems, the bandwidth surplus mode is the only mode in which the system can be self-sustaining; (2) the sequential delivery scheme is optimal in the asymptotic regime; (3) the bandwidth needed to sustain a given video in the bandwidth deficit regime grows linearly with the number of users; (4) the bandwidth needed in the surplus mode grows logarithmically with the number of peers, and is independent of the video size; (5)

the sequential peer-assisted Vo-D system is asymptotically self-sustainable and that the bandwidth needed to support it is upper bounded by the number of users times the average upload capacity of each peer.

(i) the bandwidth requested from the server is asymptotically proportional to the number of users, (ii) the server bandwidth is asymptotically independent of the peer upload bandwidth, (iii) peer-assisted VoDs become totally self-sustainable in the bandwidth surplus mode as the user population grows large.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of self-sustaining peer-assisted VoDs, and it can provide a rigorous theoretical framework to design and evaluate the performance of these systems.
the design, analysis and optimization of peer-assisted Video on Demand systems.
the design of efficient peer-assisted Video-On-Demand systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
peer-assisted VoDs are self-sustaining systems in the long term.
the peer-assisted VoV systems are self-sustaining and asymptotically optimal.
, in a peer-assisted VoV system, if the number of users is large enough, it is always possible to guarantee that the system is self-sustaining, even in the worst case.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in a peer-assisted VoV system, the number of users is a key parameter to achieve self-sustainability.
the stochastic analysis of self-sustaining systems is possible, and that the stochastic fluid approach is an effective tool to obtain such analysis.
the stochastic framework that we propose is able to capture all the main aspects of the system performance, and it can be used as a tool for system design and optimization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, under the assumption that the peer upload bandwidth distribution is known, the server bandwidth needed to support a large number of peers can be computed exactly.
, under a very general framework, peer-assisted VoDs are asymptotically self-sustaining, and that the simple sequential download scheme is optimal.

, in order to guarantee a good user experience, the server bandwidth should be chosen to be large enough to support a number of users much larger than the number of peers that are simultaneously downloading the content.
